data.question: Can an agent adopt an expired lease whose tree is measured clean without a force flag or approval?

evidence.note: research note filed, CONFIRMED by tests/test_lease_takeover.py (8 passed)
r-small-files ok (new module 3 KB), no deferred imports (guard ratchet passes), no limits or baselines raised

chunk_findings.detail: `adopt` calls `CL._claim_once(...)` and then unconditionally adds the recover-surface success keys (`found`, `_render`, `count=1`) without checking whether the claim succeeded. If `_claim_once` refuses after the earlier checks — for example, another process renews/claims the lease between the `L.scan` measurement and `_claim_once`, or the claim implementation rejects the forced takeover — the returned outcome is still a refusal, but its `data` now says `count == 1`. The comment states that the recover surface’s caps and renderer read these keys, so a failed adoption can be rendered/counted as one recovered item even though no lease was adopted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/recover_adopt.py:69-73

chunk_findings.detail: The `--adopt` branch is entered before any handling of `--plan` and calls `ddflow.api.recover_adopt.adopt` directly, without passing or checking `plan`. The declared `--plan` parameter is documented as the recovery dry run, while `--adopt` is documented to take over the lease. Thus `ddflow recover --item X --adopt --plan --reason "..."` is accepted and performs the takeover even though the user requested the dry-run/plan path; the `--plan` flag is silently ignored. A surface that exposes a dry-run flag should either reject `--adopt --plan` or propagate the dry-run request, not mutate state while pretending to plan.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:_recover_call

chunk_findings.detail: `adopt` returns `CL._claim_once(...)` unchanged, so a successful takeover has the claim outcome's kind, not `recover.adopt`. `render_recover` only special-cases `out.kind == "recover.adopt"` (the pre-claim `_refuse` path). Given a clean expired lease and a successful claim, the CLI falls through to `_render_recover` on claim-shaped data (and the injected `found`/`count`/`_render` keys), so the operator does not get the adoption line and can get a sweep render or a render error after the lease was already taken. A `_claim_once` refusal is likewise not `recover.adopt`, so the claim failure is not shown as an adopt refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/recover_adopt.py:74

chunk_findings.detail: Expiry and cleanliness are checked, then the mutation is `_claim_once(..., force=True)` with no second liveness check. `force` is what skips "held by someone else". Sequence: lease is past grace, `adopt` passes `lease.live` and the scan, the holder heartbeats and the lease is live again, then `force=True` still runs. That steals a live lease — the case the function text says it refuses — and reopens the agent force-takeover B49 closed, without `--approval`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/recover_adopt.py:46

data.probe: services/leases/claim.py _acquire_locked: a LIVE existing lease from another holder raises LeaseError before any force handling, inside decide_then_append, so force=True cannot take a lease a heartbeat renewed; force only skips the expired-lease report. tests/test_lease_takeover.py::test_a_live_lease_is_not_adopted
data.title: ddflow/api/recover_adopt.py:46

chunk_findings.detail: `adopt` calls `CL._claim_once(..., force=True)` after a non-atomic expired-lease check. If two agents call `recover --adopt` for the same expired lease, both can load state and pass `lease.live(...) == False`; the first claim succeeds, but the second still issues a forced claim and can overwrite the newly live lease. The module promises that a live lease is refused and nothing changes, but this interleaving changes a lease after it became live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/recover_adopt.py:71-75

chunk_findings.detail: After calling `_claim_once`, `adopt` unconditionally sets `out.data["count"]` to `1` without checking whether the claim actually succeeded. If `_claim_once` returns a refused outcome (for example, because the worktree became dirty after `L.scan` or the claim layer rejects the takeover), the returned outcome still reports `data["count"] == 1`, so any cap/renderer that uses `count` can report one adopted item even though none was adopted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/recover_adopt.py:71-75

chunk_findings.detail: When `--adopt` is present, `_recover_call` immediately calls `ddflow.api.recover_adopt.adopt` and never honors `a.get("plan")` (or `a.get("all")`). The existing `--plan` parameter is documented as “The triage, dry run,” so a user who runs `ddflow recover --item X --adopt --plan --reason "test"` expects no state change, but this code still performs the lease takeover and records it. The dry-run flag is silently ignored; the combination should be rejected or the plan flag should be passed through to prevent mutation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/reporting.py:_recover_call

chunk_findings.detail: The seeded `task.added` event for T1 has only `parent`, `title`, and `globs`; it does not state `needs` or carry a wave tag such as `no-deps`. The recorded rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] says every task must name its phase, state dependencies in `needs`, and carry a `wave:N` tag, with no-prerequisite tasks explicitly tagged `no-deps` so that “none” is a decision rather than an omission. This change files a task in the ddflow log without that required metadata, so the test fixture violates the project rule.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_takeover.py:_crashed

chunk_findings.detail: `adopt` returns the `_claim_once` outcome unchanged and never sets `out.kind` to `KIND` (`"recover.adopt"`). `render_recover` only prints the takeover line when `out.kind == "recover.adopt"` (`ddflow/surfaces/parsers/reporting.py:31`). After a clean expired tree is adopted, that branch is unreachable, so the surface falls through to `_render_recover` on the injected empty `found` / `_render` payload and reports a no-op sweep instead of who took the lease.
